thread.title: Is Tech Overpriced? Not These 5 Stocks

author: Nicholas Jasinski
title: Is Tech Overpriced? Not These 5 Stocks
text:
By Nicholas Jasinski Aug. 1, 2018 12:41 p.m. ET In a rough few days for FANG stocks before Tuesday’s boost, investors suddenly seem to have realized that stock valuations matters, even for tech superstars. Consider popular names such as Amazon.com (AMZN), with an average forward price/earnings (P/E) ratio of 180.9, followed by Netflix ’s (NFLX) 148.4. Those valuations can make some investors swoon, and yet they don’t even come close to the nosebleed valuation of South American e-commerce outfit MercadoLibre (MELI), which trades for 1,618.3 times earnings. Apple (AAPL) stock seems the responsible one, with a P/E of 17.5.
Illustration: Bryan Thomas/Getty Images So have other tech stock valuations come back under control? The short answer is "not quite." The average forward P/E ratio of companies in the Nasdaq 100 index, the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the tech-heavy Nasdaq Stock Market, remains a lofty 21.7, compared to 17.5 for the S&P 500, according to FactSet. Of course, not all tech companies are so pricey–but that discount is often justified. Here are the five cheapest tech stocks in the Nasdaq 100 based on their price/earnings ratio:
Micron Technology ( MU ) – P/E: 5.2
The Boise, Idaho-based NAND and DRAM flash memory-chip maker has long traded at a discount to the rest of the market. Investors have concerns over competition from cheaper rival Chinese manufacturers that threaten to oversupply the market and erode prices–and therefore Micron’s earnings. Value investors have been pounding the table for Micron to shake off its doldrums, but the stock stubbornly remains at a steep discount to other tech companies.
Western Digital ( WDC ) – P/E: 6.7
With a declining hard-disk-drive business and a NAND flash business facing the same competitive pressures as Micron’s, investors haven’t flocked to Western Digital’s stock despite growing earnings 200% over the past two years. It just turns out that when those earnings come from a declining market on one hand and an increasingly competitive market on the other, investors aren’t willing to reward the stock.
Seagate Technology ( STX ) – P/E: 10.2
Seagate shares the shrinking hard-disk-drive market with Western Digital. It has at least been able to focus on competing in that one sector, however, as Western Digital has faced additional negative investor sentiment from the threat of falling prices in its large flash storage business.
Lam Research ( LRCX ) – P/E: 10.9
Lam Research makes tools and equipment required for manufacturing DRAM and NAND flash chips. With the doom and gloom surrounding its main customers, Lam’s stock performance has been muted despite growing revenue and earnings.
Applied Materials ( AMAT ) – P/E: 11.9
Applied Materials competes with Lam to supply DRAM and NAND engineering equipment. While it continues to show sales growth, investors fear a decline in the coming years as manufacturers slow down orders.
